incidents.summary: Shareholder Samuel Tak Lee sued Shaftesbury over an allegedly improper December 2017 share placing that diluted his stake, with the company denying the claims.

sources.title: Samuel Tak Lee announces plan to vote against Shaftesbury's board at AGM
sources.quote: Lee’s legal case, which is expected to be heard in the High Court next year, alleges that Shaftesbury conducted the December 2017 share placing “improperly”.

sources.title: Capco eyes up takeover of Shaftesbury - QuotedData
sources.quote: Mr Lee launched legal action against the company last year over alleged losses from a £265m fundraising in 2017 that he says diluted his stake.

sources.title: Samuel Tak Lee announces plan to vote against Shaftesbury's board at AGM
sources.quote: Shaftesbury has denied the claims saying they have “no merit”.

incidents.summary: Shaftesbury Capital faced investor criticism over millions of pounds in executive share awards that vested upon completion of its merger.

sources.title: Covent Garden-owner Shaftesbury Capital faces bruising pay row  | Money News | Sky News
sources.quote: The newly merged property empire encompassing swathes of London’s Soho and Covent Garden is facing a bruising shareholder row over millions of pounds handed out in executive share awards.

sources.title: Covent Garden-owner Shaftesbury Capital faces bruising pay row  | Money News | Sky News
sources.quote: City investors are understood to be livid that bosses including Ian Hawksworth, its chief executive, saw share grants vest when the merger completed.

sources.title: Covent Garden-owner Shaftesbury Capital faces bruising pay row  | Money News | Sky News
sources.quote: Mr Hawksworth ran Capco, which was the acquiring entity in the merger despite being smaller, making the vesting of its share awards unusual - and controversial during a cost-of-living crisis.
